question: A 40-year-old HIV-positive patient with a CD4 count of 80 cells/µL presents with 3 weeks of progressive headache, neck stiffness and confusion. CSF analysis shows lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose and elevated protein. India ink preparation reveals encapsulated organisms with clear halos. What is the MOST sensitive rapid diagnostic test?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CrAg LFA has >99% sensitivity and >95% specificity for Cryptococcal meningitis. WHO and NACO recommend CrAg screening in all HIV patients with CD4 <100 cells/µL, even before symptoms develop, enabling early pre-emptive treatment.

VDRL detects antibodies against Treponema pallidum (syphilis). Although neurosyphilis can cause subacute meningitis, the India ink finding of encapsulated organisms with clear halos confirms Cryptococcus neoformans, not Treponema.
ASO titre detects antibodies against Streptolysin O produced by Group A Streptococcus. It is used for post-streptococcal complications (rheumatic fever, PSGN), not central nervous system infections.

Widal test detects agglutinating antibodies against Salmonella typhi O and H antigens and is used for enteric fever diagnosis. It has no role in investigating subacute meningitis with encapsulated organisms on India ink.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the OI spectrum by CD4 count. At CD4 <100, Cryptococcal meningitis must be considered in any HIV patient with subacute meningitis. India ink showing encapsulated organisms is characteristic, and CrAg LFA is the most sensitive rapid diagnostic test available.

Excellent! At CD4 <100, Cryptococcal meningitis is a leading cause of subacute meningitis in HIV. CrAg LFA is the recommended rapid point-of-care test — it can detect subclinical infection even before meningitis develops when used for screening.
